topic: التظلم الاختياري — زاوية جديدة: 3 علامات تحذيرية قبل اتخاذ القرار
prompt: A medium‑shot, slightly elevated view of a modern office desk near a window with soft daylight. In the center sits a young professional (gender‑neutral) in casual work attire, leaning slightly forward, pen in hand, focused on a stack of papers. - On the desk, the top sheet is an official‑looking decision notice (plain white paper with a faint embossed seal) placed beside a freshly drafted grievance letter, the latter covered with handwritten marginal notes and a highlighted paragraph, indicating the inclusion of new arguments. - To the right of the papers, a closed folder with a bright red label sits open, revealing a mismatched internal memo that clearly belongs to a different department (the folder’s interior shows a different color tab, suggesting it was sent to the wrong office). - In the background, a wall‑mounted analog clock shows its minute hand approaching the top of the hour, symbolizing an impending deadline. Directly above the clock hangs a small wall calendar turned to the current month; a single red sticky‑note is affixed to one of the pages, covering the date without displaying numbers, representing the critical response period. The laptop on the left displays an email draft window (no visible text), its cursor blinking, suggesting the user is preparing the optional administrative appeal. The overall composition balances the person’s attentive posture with the three visual cues—deadline clock, detailed grievance draft, and misdirected folder—conveying the careful decision‑making moment before filing the appeal. The lighting is natural from the window, complemented by a warm desk lamp that casts gentle shadows, emphasizing the paperwork and the subject’s focused expression.
